items.story: FDA Center for Veterinary Medicine updates list: no dog lifespan drug approved; newest entry is a screwworm emergency authorisation for dogs, 2026-11-03
items.note: List shows exactly the three entries claimed (2026-10-20 cefovecin skin-infection injection approval, 2026-10-27 residue-test pilot, 2026-11-03 screwworm emergency use authorisation). A check that found nothing on the tracked treatment; the one dated item in the window is unrelated to ageing.

items.story: Dog Aging Project consortium, GeroScience, 2026-11-04: study design paper for the Dog Aging Project Pack observational cohort (50,188 dogs, 14,978 deaths)
items.note: Crossref record with abstract confirms title, date and both numbers. A design paper, no drug result.

items.story: Intellia third-quarter 2026 release, 2026-11-05: enrolment complete in MAGNITUDE-2 (nex-z, nerve form, past target of 60); MAGNITUDE heart trial still enrolling; registry entries for both trials updated 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05
items.note: Bundles three things: the company release (2026-11-05), the MAGNITUDE registry update (NCT06128629, posted 2026-11-04, submitted 2026-11-02, recruiting, 1,200 estimated, primary completion 2027-12, study end 2028-04) and the MAGNITUDE-2 registry update (NCT06672237, posted 2026-11-05, submitted 2026-11-04, active not recruiting, 67 actual, primary completion 2027-07, study end 2028-08). All confirmed. The count of 138 sites was not checked. Borderline between A and B: a late-stage trial finishing enrolment is the company advancing the treatment, but there is no result and no change to the expected readout dates; the registry updates alone would be C.

items.story: VITAL-H (NCT07923630), University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio, first posted 2026-11-06: phase 2 trial of oral semaglutide, dapagliflozin or placebo in 1,200 people aged 60 to 75 against the decline of ageing
items.note: Registry confirms first posted 2026-11-06, not yet recruiting, phase 2, 1,200 people, ages 60 to 75, three arms (semaglutide oral, dapagliflozin 10 mg, placebo), collaborator Department of Health and Human Services, start 2027-01, primary completion 2030-12, study completion 2031-02, main measure the Short Physical Performance Battery. No rapamycin arm listed. Not checked: the 36 plus 6 months treatment detail, the grant marking, the exploratory biomarker outcomes, and the Texas Public Radio report of 2026-03-17 (rapamycin, 726 people).

items.story: Scribe Therapeutics release, 2026-11-04: to present updated monkey data on its PCSK9 epigenetic silencer STX-1150 (LDL cholesterol held down at least two years after one dose) at the American Heart Association meeting on 2026-11-07
items.note: The GlobeNewswire address refused (403) for me too. A news page carrying the release confirms the date, headline and content. Animal data only; the page says STX-1150 is now in a phase 1 trial in people.

items.story: Borkowski, Preprints.org, 2026-11-03: narrative review 'Artificial Intelligence in Longevity Research: From Molecular Clocks to Interventional Geroscience' (not peer reviewed)
items.note: Abstract confirms: several clocks associated with mortality; evidence for clocks as valid surrogate endpoints 'remains limited'; literature searches run in October 2026 with a separate search of FDA and EMA documents. Small detail: the abstract ties October 2026 to the literature searches, with the regulator documents searched separately.

items.story: Check for the metformin trial TAME on 2026-11-09: no registry entry posted or updated 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-09, and afar.org/research/TAME/ answers 'not found'
items.note: Both parts reproduced: the page returned 404 and the registry search returned no studies. This is a check that found nothing, not an event, so it has no date of its own and is not counted as in the window.

items.story: Loyal's page for veterinarians, read 2026-11-09: effectiveness and safety sections complete, manufacturing section and conditional approval 'In progress', STAY study ongoing; no dated news in the window
items.note: Page confirms all statuses and that the newest listed item is a GeroScience commentary of 2026-10-23. The page says the safety section was completed in December 2025. The page is undated and nothing on it is dated inside the window. The page also carries an undated banner about a milestone for a different Loyal drug (LOY-003), which no reader mentioned and I did not follow up.

items.story: American Heart Association release, 2026-11-02, on meeting abstract MDP1524: in records of 256,492 adults with prediabetes and obesity, GLP-1 drug users had fewer heart attacks, strokes and deaths than metformin users
items.note: All numbers confirmed: 256,492 adults, 15 per cent fewer heart attacks, 20 per cent fewer strokes, 41 per cent lower risk of death, about three years, meeting 2026-11-06 to 2026-11-09 in Chicago, abstract not peer reviewed. Observational, with metformin as the comparison drug.

items.story: Epirium Bio, registry entry NCT07921420 first posted 2026-11-06: phase 2b placebo-controlled trial of MF-300 in 225 adults aged 65 and over with age-related muscle loss
items.note: Registry confirms title, sponsor, not yet recruiting, 225 people, age 65 and over, main measure the five-times chair-stand test, start 2027-01-01, primary completion 2028-06-01. Not checked: the 24-week duration, the open first part, and the drug's target (15-PGDH). Graded A as a new mid-stage trial in people plainly aimed at an ageing condition; it is not one of the site's own treatments (not a mitochondria drug), so B is defensible.

items.story: Scribe Therapeutics release, 2026-11-04: to present monkey data on STX-1150 at the American Heart Association meeting on 2026-11-07
items.note: Same release as S1167. Summary page confirms at least two years of LDL cholesterol control in monkeys after one dose and the presentation on 2026-11-07.

items.story: Zheng and colleagues, Journal of Nutrition, Health and Aging, online 2026-11-07: faster biological age from routine blood tests linked to aortic valve narrowing in two groups (4,526 and 5,114 people)
items.note: Europe PMC gives first publication 2026-11-07 and confirms both group sizes and that biological age came from clinical blood markers (two standard methods), not DNA marks. Crossref shows the licence starting 2026-10-23 and the print issue as February 2027, so the article may have been available slightly earlier than 2026-11-07.

items.story: Mostafaei, Lindh, Qin, Mak and Hagg, Research Square preprint, 2026-11-04: biological age measures and death from any cause in TwinGene (9,617) and UK Biobank (314,064)
items.note: All numbers confirmed: 11 to 27 per cent (TwinGene) and 24 to 40 per cent (UK Biobank) higher hazard per standard deviation, so 11 to 40 per cent overall; prediction score 0.780 to 0.787 and 0.720 to 0.746. Not peer reviewed.

items.story: Niewisch and colleagues, PLOS Genetics, 2026-11-05: how common inherited TERT (telomerase gene) variants are in the population and which illnesses go with them
items.note: Title 'Genomic ascertainment refines the population prevalence and phenotype associations of germline TERT variants' and date confirmed. The UK Biobank and DiscovEHR detail was not checked (no abstract in the record). Background, not a treatment study.

items.story: Chen and colleagues, Cardiovascular Diabetology, 2026-11-02: 'Biological age acceleration, plasma proteomics, and incident arrhythmias in type 2 diabetes'
items.note: Title and date confirmed in Crossref only; no abstract read, as the reader also said.

items.story: Mizoguchi and colleagues (Verve Therapeutics, part of Eli Lilly), Nature, 2026-11-06: laboratory and monkey work for a one-dose base editor that switches off ANGPTL3; first trial in people under way
items.note: Abstract confirms more than 90 per cent fall in the protein in monkeys lasting three years after one dose, no off-target editing at about 3,000 candidate sites, and an ongoing first trial in people with hard-to-treat high blood fats. No result in people. One claim adds a second story: a CRISPR Therapeutics meeting talk on CTX310 scheduled for 2026-11-09, which that reader did not open and I did not check.

items.story: Journal of Clinical Investigation, 2026-11-02: dapagliflozin linked to lower odds of pre-frail older people with high blood pressure and kidney disease becoming frail over one year (odds ratio 0.13), matched comparison, not randomised
items.note: Abstract confirms 135 enrolled, 105 left after matching (52 on the drug), odds ratio 0.130, one year. The two claims differ only in quoting 135 or 105; both numbers are right for what they describe. The 'over 65' detail was not checked.

items.story: Biological Psychiatry, online 2026-11-07: post-traumatic stress disorder linked to older readings on five DNA-mark clocks in 43,155 United States veterans
items.note: Abstract confirms 43,155 veterans, five clocks, up to about two years on GrimAge. The Million Veteran Program detail was not checked. An association with clock readings, not a test of a clock predicting death or disease.

items.story: Intellia announces enrolment complete in the late-stage MAGNITUDE-2 trial of nex-z (nerve form), 2026-11-04
items.note: News page dated 2026-11-04 confirms about 60 adults, one dose against placebo, end points at month 18 (nerve score) and day 29 (protein level), and links to a company wire release of 2026-11-04, which I did not open. Same event as the enrolment news in S1035, where the company's results release of 2026-11-05 repeats it.

items.story: Diaz-Vallejo and colleagues, GeroScience, 2026-11-04: systematic review of randomised trials of polyphenol supplements and muscle in adults aged 55 and over; five completed trials, inconsistent effects
items.note: Abstract confirms. Compounds named are quercetin, epicatechin-rich extracts, tea catechins, cocoa flavonoids and marine polyphenols; urolithin A is not among them.

items.story: Ye and colleagues, Cell Stem Cell, 2026-11-05: lasting, partly reversible silencing of a platelet gene by editing DNA marks in human blood-forming stem cells, stable four months after transplant into mice
items.note: Abstract confirms the gene (ITGB3), primary human blood-forming stem cells, four months in mice, partial reversal by a targeted second edit. Laboratory and animal work, no person treated.

items.story: Galkina and colleagues, Food & Function, 2026-11-02: in 104 older adults in a two-year walnut-diet trial, rises in urolithins went with preserved thickness of the brain's outer layer
items.note: Abstract confirms 104 people (55 on walnuts), the two-year WAHA trial, and the association in the walnut group. An association inside a diet trial, on the brain, not a drug trial on muscle.

items.story: Intellia third-quarter 2026 release, 2026-11-05: MAGNITUDE-2 enrolment complete, heart trial enrolling, immune-gene test results given to doctors; restates the 2027-03-10 decision date for lonvo-z (hereditary angioedema)
items.note: Same release as S1035. Bundles a second story: the regulator's decision date for lonvo-z of 2027-03-10, priority review, no advisory committee planned, launch planned for the first quarter of 2027. All confirmed in the release, which makes no mention of a clinical hold or liver safety. The lonvo-z acceptance is older news restated (one reader dates it 2026-09-08; not checked), and the disease is not age-related.

items.story: Tune Therapeutics news page, item of 2026-11-05: its editing platform TEMPO named gene editing platform of the year in an industry awards scheme; no new clinical data
items.note: News listing confirms the award item and its date. The listing also shows items of 2026-06-05, 2026-06-10 and 2026-10-05, so the claim that nothing followed the release of 2026-05-30 is not exact; those items look like press coverage and a company-ranking mention, not new data, a paper or a phase 2 start.

items.story: Grenville and colleagues, medRxiv preprint, 2026-11-04: markers of ageing in childhood and lung function over time in a UK birth cohort
items.note: Confirmed. DNA-mark age measures showed little link with low lung function; three inflammation proteins did. Not a test of a clock predicting death or disease, and only loosely about ageing.

items.story: Stealth BioTherapeutics, registry entry NCT07531251 (4TAZPower) updated 2026-11-09: placebo-controlled confirming trial of elamipretide in 48 people with Barth syndrome, recruiting
items.note: Registry confirms update posted 2026-11-09 (submitted 2026-11-05), recruiting, 48 people, 72 weeks, start 2026-07-02, primary completion 2029-09-30, aim to confirm benefit. What changed in the update was not established. A rare disease, not age-related muscle loss.

items.story: Bautista and Lopez-Cortes, Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine, 2026-11-09: 'Toward a vascular mitochondrial clock of biological aging', a conceptual piece
items.note: Title and date confirmed in Crossref; the abstract describes a conceptual framework, not a cohort report.
